__doc__: Planner-level exemplar for the visual-product-search app archetype. Documents the entities, pages, agent-graph, and integrations the planner should emit when a brief matches this archetype (see services.app_design_catalog.classify_app_archetype). Used both as documentation and as a few-shot exemplar in the planner prompt. Slice 4 supplies the concrete /scan page schema at backend/services/schema_examples/scan/visual_scan.json (assumed path — Slice 4 owns it).
name: PriceScan
description: Users scan/upload a product photo; the app identifies it via Claude vision and returns live prices from admin-approved retailers via the Firecrawl MCP server.

entities.name: scan_events
entities.description: One row per user scan; holds the uploaded image, the Claude-identified product, and the retailer matches.

entities.name: retail_sources
entities.description: Admin-controlled allow-list of retailers the app-agent is permitted to query.

fields.name: source_key
fields.description: Stable key referenced by the agent guardrail, e.g. 'amazon_us'

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Lower = higher priority in the results ordering.

pages.name: ScanPage
pages.description: Mobile-first camera + upload surface that calls the app agent (see agent_graph) and renders match cards.

pages.name: RetailSourcesListPage
pages.description: Admin list of retail sources with per-row enable/disable toggle, priority, region, and edit/delete actions.

pages.name: RetailSourceCreatePage
pages.description: Admin form to add a new retail source (name, source_key, url, enabled, priority, region).

pages.name: RetailSourceEditPage
pages.description: Admin form to edit an existing retail source.

agent_graph.name: PriceScanAgent
agent_graph.description: Identifies products from a scanned image and returns live prices from admin-approved retailers via the Firecrawl MCP server.

system_prompt.prompt: You identify products from images and return live prices from admin-approved retailers. Return JSON of shape {product: {brand, model, category, attributes, confidence}, matches: [{title, price, currency, seller, url, image}]}. If confidence < 0.5, return matches: [] and a friendly message.

tools.name: identify_product
tools.description: Given the uploaded image file_id, identify the product via Claude vision (ai_extract with image input) and return {brand, model, category, attributes, confidence}.
tools.code: // materialised by code_editor — reads forge_files[image_id], calls ai_extract with the identify_product_from_image preset, returns typed JSON

tools.name: search_prices
tools.description: Discover candidate product URLs across retailers via Firecrawl search. Returns [{title, url, description}]. Feed each result's `url` into `extract_price` — search alone does not return prices.

tools.name: extract_price
tools.description: Extract structured {productUrl, price, currency, inStock} from a specific retailer product page. Call once per candidate URL from search_prices. Product pages parse reliably; search-result pages (amazon.com/s?k=..., target.com/s?searchTerm=...) parse ~30-50% of the time — always pass a product/detail URL, not a search URL. Two-step flow is O7 in the pipeline remediation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-generation-pipeline-remediation.md).

args_mapping.prompt: Extract the primary offer price for the exact product page.

rules.name: seller_in_enabled_sources
rules.expr: match.seller in retail_sources WHERE enabled=true; order by retail_sources.priority asc

mcp_servers.name: Firecrawl
mcp_servers.description: Shopping-search + scrape MCP server used by the product_identifier agent to fetch live retailer prices.
